about: The home of Mojo, a new programming language for fast code, and Modular's tools for running AI models.

prs.title: Splitting text into lines no longer drops a line
prs.broken: When text mixed old-style Mac line breaks with normal ones, Mojo's split-into-lines function silently lost a line. "a, b, c" came back as "a, c".
prs.changed: I fixed a check meant to skip only empty pieces, so it no longer skips real lines.
prs.matters: Programs reading text from different systems get every line, the same as Python gives.

prs.title: Tests in a loop now check every round, not just the first
prs.broken: Mojo has a test helper that checks code crashes when it should. In a loop it re-ran the first round each time, so tests could pass having checked one case.
prs.changed: I made it count how many times each check has been reached, so every round runs its own case.
prs.matters: A test that reports a pass has now really checked every case it claims to.

prs.title: A stuck test now fails instead of hanging forever
prs.broken: Mojo's helper for testing deliberate crashes waited forever if the code froze instead of crashing. The whole test run stalled with no hint of which test was stuck.
prs.changed: I added a time limit, 60 seconds by default, after which it stops the stuck code and fails that test with its output.
prs.matters: Developers get a clear failure they can fix, instead of a frozen test run killed with no explanation.

prs.title: Raising a number to a huge whole power now gives the right answer
prs.broken: In Mojo, raising a decimal number to a whole power above about two billion, or to infinity, always gave 1. So 0.5 to the power of 4 billion gave 1 instead of 0, and could even crash.
prs.changed: Powers that fit the fast path still use it. Bigger or infinite ones now go through a general formula that handles them correctly, with tests for both sizes of number.
prs.matters: Math code that uses very large powers gets real results instead of a silent 1 or a crash.

prs.title: Splitting text into lines no longer breaks on tabs
prs.broken: In Mojo, splitting text into lines also split at every tab. Tab-separated data like a table fell apart into single cells.
prs.changed: Tabs are no longer treated as line ends, matching Python. The help text that listed tabs as line ends was fixed too, and a test was added.
prs.matters: Code that reads tab-separated text line by line gets whole rows back.

prs.title: Reversing a span in Mojo gives the right order at every length
prs.broken: Reversing a span scrambled it for many lengths, such as 2, 5 and 6. The fast loop left a few pairs that the cleanup step swapped wrongly or skipped.
prs.changed: The leftover pairs are now swapped one by one up to the middle. A new test reverses every length from 0 to 39.
prs.matters: Code that reverses a buffer of numbers gets a correct result instead of silently wrong data.

prs.title: Extending a Mojo deque with an empty list no longer crashes
prs.broken: Adding an empty list to a deque, at either end or when building one, crashed the program while freeing memory the list never had.
prs.changed: The deque now skips freeing when the list never held anything, the same way the list type itself does.
prs.matters: Programs that pass a possibly empty list into a deque keep running.
